name: AD7150BRMZ-REEL
title: Two-channel ultralow-power capacitance-to-digital converter for proximity sensing
summary: The AD7150 measures two floating capacitive sensors, each wired between an excitation output (EXC1, EXC2) and a converter input (CIN1, CIN2), with a sigma-delta capacitance-to-digital converter and compares each result against a threshold. The threshold is either a fixed value or follows a running average of the data, so slow drift from humidity, temperature or ageing of the dielectric is ignored while a fast change sets the channel's output, OUT1 or OUT2. At power-up it works on its own with factory settings; over its I2C-compatible interface a host can change every setting and read data and status. It runs from 2.7 V to 3.6 V at about 100 µA and comes in a 10-lead MSOP.
key_figures: 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 pF, offset up to 10 pF min by CAPDAC
1.0 fF to 2.0 fF typ by range
10 ms for both channels, 5 ms per channel
I2C compatible, 400 kHz, write address 0x90, read 0x91

notes: Z marks a RoHS-compliant part. AD7150BRMZ-REEL is the same part as AD7150BRMZ on a reel.

operation.text: The converter is a charge-balancing sigma-delta modulator of second order followed by a digital filter of third order. During a conversion the excitation drives one plate of the sensor CX and the modulator samples the charge passing through it; the filter turns the bit stream into a 12-bit result that feeds the comparators and can be read over the bus. Both plates of the sensor must float: neither may be tied to ground or any fixed potential. The excitation edge is slew-limited, which lowers its harmonics and improves EMC.

The converter's largest range is 4 pF. A 6-bit, monotonic on-chip CAPDAC acts as a negative capacitance on CIN and cancels up to 10 pF of fixed sensor capacitance, so with the CAPDAC set to 10 pF the 4 pF range covers 10 pF to 14 pF of sensor.

OUT1 and OUT2 are active high. In fixed mode the data is compared with a constant threshold and the output reports any crossing. In adaptive mode the threshold tracks an average of past data, so the output reacts to fast changes, such as a hand approaching the sensor, and ignores slow ones from humidity, temperature or dielectric ageing. Positive and negative modes flag a rise or a fall; adaptive mode adds in-window and out-window modes.

In adaptive mode each threshold sits a programmed distance, 0 to 255 LSBs of the 12-bit result, above and/or below the average. The comparator then has hysteresis of a quarter of the sensitivity, which can be switched off; fixed mode has none.

After a large, lasting change the average may take too long to catch up. A timeout counts conversions while the data stays outside average ± sensitivity; when it runs out the average, and so the thresholds, jump to the present data and the history is dropped. Approaching (toward the threshold) and receding (away from it) timeouts are set separately.

In adaptive mode with AutoDAC on, the CAPDAC steps up when the average goes over three quarters of full range and down when it drops under one quarter, keeping the converter in its best range. The step size follows the chosen input range.
The part can power itself down after a programmed time without any output going active. A serial command or cycling the supply brings it back.

When VDD falls below the level the converter needs (2.45 V typ), the monitor holds the adaptive threshold logic in reset; once VDD recovers, the average restarts from the first good conversion. This keeps a slow supply ramp or a dip from leaving a wrong threshold. Other functions carry on down to roughly 1.0 V to 1.8 V, depending on process, with the bus still working, but results taken under the threshold are not valid. The PwrDown status bit shows the monitor's state.

A data register updates after each finished conversion, except while it is being read over the bus, when the new result is lost. A read ends at the stop condition, so read both bytes in one auto-incrementing transaction (four bytes with both channels enabled) to avoid mixing two results. The average registers hold the running average in the same format. The fixed-threshold values occupy the same addresses as the sensitivity and timeout values and are unreachable in adaptive mode.

The interface is I2C compatible, with the AD7150 always a slave. Its address byte is 0x90 for a write and 0x91 for a read. In a write the byte after the address is the register pointer; any following bytes go to successive registers as the pointer auto-increments, and a stop returns the pointer to 0x00. In a read the part sends the addressed register and moves on to the next each time the master acknowledges; with no acknowledge it returns to idle without incrementing. After a read ending in a stop, the pointer goes back to the status register, so status can be polled without rewriting the pointer. Writes to an invalid address are acknowledged and discarded; reads past the map keep returning internal contents until the master sends no-acknowledge, start or stop. The pointer itself cannot be read.

Writing the pointer value 0xBF resets the part and reloads all defaults without resetting the bus. A general call (address 0x00, write) followed by 0x06 does the same. During the reload, about 2 ms, the part does not acknowledge. Other general-call commands are not acknowledged.

The sensor connects straight between EXC and CIN. Standalone, the part runs on its power-up defaults and signals on OUT1 and OUT2; with a microcontroller on the bus, the host can overwrite the registers with its own setup.

Capacitance from CIN or EXC to ground ideally has no effect but changes the result gradually; the limits are 100 pF on CIN and 300 pF on EXC. Leakage from the sensor to ground also shifts the result, so keep the sensor isolated from ground with as much resistance as possible (at least 10 MΩ on CIN, 1 MΩ on EXC). Resistance across the sensor passes charge and reads as extra capacitance. Series resistance (RS1 + RS2, CIN side plus EXC side) should be in the hundreds of ohms; the specified limit is 125 kΩ.

CIN has internal ESD protection. Any added overvoltage or EMC parts in the sensor path must stay within the limits on capacitance to ground, series resistance and leakage. One input filter that greatly improves immunity to high-frequency noise at the cost of a little extra gain and offset error: 39 kΩ then 82 kΩ in series from the sensor to CIN, with 68 pF to ground after the 39 kΩ and 22 pF to ground at CIN, and 10 kΩ in series from the sensor to EXC with 47 pF to ground at EXC.

Power-supply rejection is good at dc and low frequency, but ripple and noise near the excitation frequency and its harmonics can disturb the part. A filter of 1 kΩ in series from the supply to VDD, with 0.1 µF and 10 µF from VDD to ground, improves immunity. When the bus also serves other circuits, connect the SDA and SCL pull-ups (1 kΩ) on the supply side of that 1 kΩ; when the bus is unused in standalone mode, connect them directly to VDD.

circuits.title: Standalone operation
circuits.description: A 3 V battery powers the AD7150 with a 0.1 µF capacitor across VDD. Two sensors sit between EXC1 and CIN1 and between EXC2 and CIN2. SDA and SCL are pulled up to VDD by 1 kΩ each and nothing else uses them, so the part runs on its defaults. OUT1 lights LED2 and OUT2 lights LED1, each through 1 kΩ to ground, when the channel detects proximity.

circuits.title: Interfaced to a host microcontroller
circuits.description: The AD7150 and a host microcontroller share a 3.3 V rail; 0.1 µF decouples VDD. SDA and SCL run to the host's bus pins with a 1 kΩ pull-up each to 3.3 V, so the host can set the registers and read data and status. OUT1 and OUT2 go to the host's IRQ1 and IRQ2 inputs. Two sensors sit between EXC1 and CIN1 and between EXC2 and CIN2.

circuits.title: Standalone operation with EMC protection
circuits.description: An ADP1720-3.3 regulator, with 1 µF at its input and at its output, makes 3.3 V from VSUPPLY. The AD7150 takes its VDD through a 1 kΩ resistor with 0.1 µF and 10 µF to ground, which filters supply noise near the excitation frequency. The 1 kΩ SDA and SCL pull-ups go to the 3.3 V side of that resistor, and both lines leave the circuit for other users of the bus. Each sensor reaches CIN through 39 kΩ and 82 kΩ with 68 pF and 22 pF to ground, and EXC through 10 kΩ with 47 pF to ground, for immunity to high-frequency noise. OUT1 and OUT2 each drive an n-channel MOSFET (Q1, Q2) whose drain, pulled up to VSUPPLY by R1 or R2, gives an active-low output at the supply level.
